The training that brought me back to life 😍 Well, holy fuck, what an experience. ❤️

I’ve just finished another Wild Love Breathwork & Leadership Training, and I don’t quite know how to put into words what these last two weeks have meant to me.

There was so much beauty in this group. So much laughter, tenderness, discomfort, courage, honesty and love. We had women from their early twenties to almost sixty, all bringing their own experiences, wisdom and wonderfully human shit into the room.

And we went places together.

I watched women find their voices, take up more space, soften towards themselves, open to pleasure and joy, & begin imagining lives that feel so much more like their own.

One woman said she came to Wild Love to learn breathwork & ended up learning how to have a love affair with life.

I mean… 🥹

But something else happened for me in this training too.

For the first time in a long time, I really allowed myself to receive the beauty of what we’ve created. To feel proud of it. To recognise how much I’ve grown as a teacher & how much this work has grown alongside me.

I’ve spent years telling people that I’m just the guide, that they’re the ones doing the healing… & of course they are. But I’m beginning to understand that I can also acknowledge the love, care, knowledge and years of my life that have gone into creating these spaces.

And that feels really fucking good.

This year hasn’t been the easiest for me personally or professionally, but somehow we’ve delivered three of our most beautiful trainings yet.

I’m finishing this one feeling grounded, deeply grateful, incredibly proud, & more in love with this work than ever.

10000 Thank you’s @jourdi_bleu & @reneelittle for your presence and support in all the ways.

To the women who trusted us with their hearts, to my two incredible apprentices who held me as beautifully as they held everyone else, and to every person who has helped shape Wild Love into what it is today, THANKYOU!

What a strange, magnificent, messy, beautiful thing it is to be human.

And what a privilege to get to do this work. ❤️

4 years ago I had what I now know as a SIM (SkyDaddy Intervention Moment) … 

“Put the drink down for good & watch your wildest dreams come true” 

We’re the words that filled my head as I was giving myself a pep talk in the car mirror before having to step in the studio to teach a yoga class 🪞 

I was hungover {again} even though I had promised myself I was done with this feeling more times than I’d like to admit 

The guilt, shame & inauthenticity was so dense & unbearable in my body it caused me to shutter in disgust with myself 

In that moment, I remember sensing a fork in the road .. 

I had realised years before then that my relationship with alcohol wasn’t “normal” or healthy by any standard

But my “drinking thinking” and ability to mask what was really happening inside of me kept justifying reasons why I could moderate … why I deserve to celebrate with my friends on the weekend … and how classy a woman appeared when she knew how to order a good glass of wine that paired with her meal perfectly 💁🏼‍♀️

But now I know that was my addict part trying to stay alive, trying to get her way. Because numbing was safe in some ways. It served me for so many years and let’s be honest - there was also a lot of fun that came along with it 

So one path was to stay on that roller coaster and see where it took me 👆🏼

And the other path was to step into my power fully 💫

To own the fact that it’s okay to not be okay, admit I had a problem & ask for more help 

This path includes travelling the world to share healing modalities & being the light when all people can see is the darkness ✨

4 years ago today, I chose the latter path, and I haven’t drank since 

Has it been easy?
Hell no

Worth it? 
Best choice I’ve ever had the courage to make 💥 

I’m still a beautiful, messy, fun, playful, raw work in progress, but I am taking care of myself better than I ever have, and I know it’s only gonna get better & better & better ✨

Thank you to my family, friends & coaches along the way who believed in me when I didn’t believe in myself yet ❣️

If I can, so can you 💜

I used to think a life like this was something that happened to other people.

The travelling. The freedom. The unexpected opportunities. The feeling that life is actually working with you.

And I think a big part of what’s changed is that I stopped treating those things like they were too good to be true.

I started letting myself believe they were possible for me.

Not just in a “one day, when everything is perfect” kind of way.

But in the way I make decisions. The way I show up. The way I respond when something doesn’t go to plan.

The way I let myself receive.

And the way I keep choosing to believe that there is more available to me than what I can currently see.

Because your beliefs don’t just shape what you think is possible.

They shape what you notice. What you’re willing to try. What you’re willing to receive. And, over time, the reality you create.

And honestly?

It’s been really frickin  beautiful to watch that unfold.

Not because everything always goes my way.

But because I’m no longer waiting for everything to go my way before I let myself feel like life is good.

I’m learning to embody the belief that it can be good now.

That I can trust myself.

That I can create a life I love.

That I can be supported.

That I can have more than I once thought was possible.

And the more I live from that place, the more I seem to find evidence that it’s true.

So if you’re in a season where your current reality doesn’t quite match the life you know you want…

Maybe you don’t need to have it all figured out yet.

Maybe you just need to start practising the belief that it’s possible.

And then let your life catch up. 💞

Your beliefs create your reality. And when you start embodying that? Fuck, it gets good my love 🚀

I’ve moved through the whole range of emotions regarding my participation in Below Deck. 

But ultimately, I trust that it all happened exactly as it was meant to, and now I’m so grateful for that experience. 

Watching those episodes 2 and a half years ago was a huge reason why I have put booze down for good. 

I say “for good”, because I honestly don’t think about drinking in the slightest now. I can get offered one of my old favorites and I don’t even have a twinge of desire to put them on my lips anymore. 

However, I never want to get complacent, as I know my “drinking thinking” is deeply engrained in my subconscious and has potential to be reactivated. 

But the more work I do to fire up new neuropathways, new habit loops and new ways of thinking and being, the more I really believe I won’t go back to drinking ever again. 
 
I celebrated 28 months yesterday without a drink. And I truly am living a life beyond my wildest dreams now because of that choice 💫

I am currently in an Alchemy container with my coach @jodydontjecoaching and this year is about radical self acceptance and owning ALL parts of me. 

Posting about being on Below Deck is extremely significant for me. I am fully owning, accepting and loving the wild child party girl Jourdi and all that she is. 

She was just doing the best she could with  what she knew at the time. And I have so much love for her now 🥰

The more I human, the more wild of an experience I believe it is. We pile these stories on to ourselves that have so many emotions involved, and they can become incredibly heavy and real. 

But what I believe is really real is who I truly am - divine wisdom and infinite love 💕 

I now know deep down without a doubt that I am a thread in the unified field that strings us all together 🪡

And my life path this time around is to shed these stories and layers of who I am not, to bring me closer to who I truly am ✨

So this is me - shedding the guilt and the shame associated with my wild child party girl Jourdi like a snake 🐍 shedding its old skin. 

Thanks for reading my story 🙏🏼

Part 2: 

Welp, the day filming commenced I was pretty hungover from my Airlie Beach run around. I boarded the yacht and they handed me my mocktail (as I had originally asked for on the preference sheet), but my “drinking thinking” convinced me that wasn’t going to cut it for the next 3 days we were on board … 

“It is my 30th birthday after all and I deserve to have some drinks! What’s the big deal anyways Jourdi …” -  my drinking thinking thoughts. 

I discreetly pulled one of the staff members aside and told them things had changed, that I’m actually drinking again but I would rather them not make a big deal of it… 

Watching my episodes air to the world a year later was pretty heart wrenching … 

I happened to be visiting my family in the USA when they came out. I remember sitting on my Uncles couch in Chicago with my entire family as the much anticipated scenes played on the screen in front of us. 

When I realized what sort of creative story lines the editors had spun for entertainment purposes (as they do in all reality TV), my stomach sank. I ran to the bathroom and broke down in hysterical tears. 

There I was … shown to be the only one ordering tons of drinks on board, being portrayed as the girl who wasn’t gonna drink and then drank … 

I knew I had agreed to go on the show with all the stipulations that came along with it, but watching it unfold live on TV was the deepest humiliation I had ever felt. I remember going to bed that night and actually wishing it was all a bad dream that I would wake up from. My deepest vulnerability of having a drinking problem was now splattered on screen in plain sight for the entire world to see. 

My 15 mins of fame was my worst nightmare… 

The shame and guilt were pretty unbearable and had a strong grip over me until recently. It wasn’t just about being on the show in that light, these wounds ran extremely deep for me. This was the cherry on top of my shame/guilt cupcake that had been baking inside of me as a result of the last 15 years of my drinking career…

I thought it was gonna be my 15 mins of fame … 

And it kinda was, but not in the way I originally planned it to be. 

When I got invited to go on Below Deck Down Under Season 1 as a Primary Charter guest, I was in my phase of drinking/not drinking. 

If you’ve ever had a problematic relationship with booze, you get it. It’s a journey. And for most people on this path, there’s a phase where it’s hard to fully accept that you’re just way better without drinking at all. 

I was in this period where I would be sober for a month or two or three, but then that one party would come and I would give in. When I would give in, the “drinking thinking” had a bit of a hold over me. I would tell myself all sorts of stories about how I could moderate, how it wasn’t that bad, how everyone got a little too drunk sometimes … 

When I filled out the preference sheet of what sort of food/drinks I wanted on board 3 months before filming, I was hell bent on not drinking. I was going to go on world wide TV and show the globe that you could celebrate your 30th birthday booze free and still have the time of your life. So with this in mind, I ordered non-alcoholic wines, AF beers and mocktail margs.

I was so determined to be the fun loving booze-free babe and inspire people to get on the AF band wagon.  I actually didn’t have any alcohol up until a couple days before filming, so I was sober for about a 4 month stint that time. 

I had never been on a holiday without drinking (which again, if you’ve ever been on the AF journey, you know  that this is a pretty big “first”). Part of the deal was that we went up there a few days before filming to settle into a lux 5 star resort on the beach. 

The easy going, fun, beachy party scene of Airlie Beach was such a vibe. The moment we got off the plane, I caved. I was in celebration mode with my friends and the night clubs and pina coladas were too much for me to resist. 

I told myself “it’s okay, I’ll just have a few fun nights and then not drink on the yacht as originally planned” …

It’s been 2 years today since I had my last drink 🙅🏼‍♀️🍷

Reminder - it didn’t stick right away. 6 years ago I first realized alcohol “might” be an issue for me 

I say “might” because drinking changes the way we think. At that stage, I was drinking everyday and usually would start around lunchtime if I could. And back then my drinking thinking convinced me that this was fine, it wasn’t an issue, I just loved my rose with my lunch right?! lol 🤦🏼‍♀️

So here’s the tips that I can give you to put down the booze for good if you’re on the roller coaster 🎢 

1. Your life is going to have to change a little bit. Can you still go out? Ya sure. But I would avoid social situations until you feel strong enough to be in them and also - you probably won’t want to spend countless hours talking absolutely nonsense at the pub. Your priorities (maybe including your friends) will change and that’s OKAY 

2. Make friends who don’t drink and find sober events. There’s a whole community of people out there who still have tons of fun without booze. If you don’t know any, hit me up - I can introduce you 😘

3. Do more things that make you feel ALIVE ✨ AKA sunrises 🌅 (and not from pushing through from the night before 🤣) The better you feel without booze, the more likely you will be to stay away from it 

4. If you’re serious about stopping drinking, seek some help from a coach, a therapist, or do some deep breath work sessions. Heavy drinking is a symptom of something deeper happening, most of the time we are drinking to escape feeling something. Getting to the bottom of this is crucial for long term booze free living (in my humble opinion 🙏🏼) 

So incredibly grateful I had the courage to put it down for good 2 years ago today. That day I was hungover AGAIN after promising myself I wouldn’t be anymore. My eyes were filled with shame and guilt when I looked into the mirror cuz I knew I wasn’t living up to my fullest potential. I closed my eyes cuz it was too unbearable to look at the girl staring back at me. I deepened my breath and I heard a voice “Put the drink down for good and watch your wildest dreams come true”

What is Rebirthing Breath Work? 

It’s a big question because it can mean so many different things to different people 

So let me break it down 👇🏼

There are 3 main components: 

1. We are breathing for about 45 mins - 1 hour. We do conscious connected breaths, which means we eliminate the pause at the top of the inhale and bottom of the exhale, making a circular ⭕️ shape with the breath. We typically breath in and out of the nose 👃 

2. Emotional release is very common. We store emotions and trauma in the physical body and when we breathe in this way, we access our subconscious minds. It will show us past memories, or bring up old situations that we are ready to heal from. Since you have to feel to heal, this is one of the most effective ways to remove emotional blockages that you might not even be aware are running your life 🙅🏼‍♀️

3. Access to Oneness, spirit, the divine love and light {insert your word for Higher Power here} is extremely common. Almost everyone that I have met who does this breath work has some experience of lightness, a sense of calmness, an overwhelming feeling of home. The more you visit this space within, the easier it becomes to access. And this space, my loves, is where all the magic happens ✨

Rebirthing is for you if: 

💥 You’re ready to release unhealthy habits that you know aren’t serving you anymore 
💥 You find yourself repeating a pattern (same relationship, same emotional reaction, etc.) and you don’t understand why 
💥 You are wanting to experience direct access to a more calm, cool & collected space within 
💥 You are feeling lost and are seeking some answers on your next best steps 
💥 You are suffering from an overactive mind and want a little break from the swirling thoughts

So being back and settling into a new home and a new phase of my career stirred up some emotions for me the other day 

I felt the tears coming and instead of avoiding them and moving on with my day, I decided to give myself the space to feel

 I felt what was there to be felt as I let the music move my body 

I ran my hands over myself, giving feather tickles in a loving, soft way

Giving myself the love that I was seeking in that moment 

I wasn’t even fully aware of the stories attached to the emotions 

But I let them move through me, out of me 

I accepted that they were there, acknowledged them, thanked them and then let them go 

And then I picked up right where I left off and continued on with my day feeling lighter 

Emotions only have a 90 second physiological effect on the body

Everything you experience after that is just the ego attaching stories to the emotion and keeping you in a loop 

The real flex happens when you let yourself move through these things as they arise instead of pushing them down ✨👐🏼

I often get asked HOW to start the journey of coming home to yourself ✨

The simple answer is - you need to begin to quiet the monkey mind 🙉 

The simplest way to do that is by dropping into your body 

Here’s 6 things I do regularly to do that: 

1. Breath work 🌬️ - it’s one of the things we take for granted the most because it happens automatically. But when you learn different techniques of breath control, it’s literally life changing 

2. Yoga & Meditation 🧘‍♀️- an ancient wisdom - there’s a reason this has been passed down for over 5000 years. It has survived the test of time because it works! 

3. Earthing🌲 🐾 - walking barefoot outside and connecting to Mama Gaia. There’s all sorts of science behind the benefits of transferring the Earths electrons through the ground and into the body 

4. Workout 🏋️- running, weights, HIIT class, spin … pick something that you enjoy doing and sweat it out regularly. It releases all the happy hormones 🙃

5. Dancing 💃- it’s been part of ancient cultures for generations for a reason. It shakes the energy up, and reminds you not to take yourself so seriously. Your inner child will thank you ☺️ 

6. Cold Water Therapy 🧊- there’s a reason it’s the hot new trend! Ice baths, cold pool plunges, cold showers, chilly ocean/river dips .. submerge yourself in the icy-ness for 2 mins. Physical benefits aside, it teaches your subconscious that you can do hard things 💪🏼

Do you do any of these? 👇🏼

I visited my old favourite - Strawberry Park Hot Springs - a couple nights ago. For those of you who aren’t from Colorado, they are beautiful natural hot spring pools and at night you can visit under the stars for a clothing optional dip 😜
.
I was so excited to get back to this spot, as I have a lot of memories there. But as I walked down the dirt path to get in the warm springs, I felt super uncomfortable. My heart started beating a little faster as those old memories flooded back in 💬
.
I realised that this was the first time I had been there sober. All the other times I visited this place at night, I was pretty off my chops on booze or substances. All this guilt and shame came bubbling to the surface as I recalled how I was behaving there all those previous visits 🫣
.
I sat with this uncomfortableness for awhile, and then I closed my eyes. I envisioned the previous version of me there, intoxicated and acting silly. I looked at her with so much compassion. She just wanted to feel love and connection, and she felt that the booze got her there faster. She was hurting deep inside, hence why she was so reckless 🫨
.
She was my fairy with broken wings 🪽 
.
I envisioned myself holding her hand and then pulled her onto my lap and gave her a big hug. She was doing the best she could with what she knew back then 💓
.
It’s been a game changer in my healing process to have more compassion for these older versions of me. Instead of despising her and cringing at her, accepting her and loving her, because she’s a part of me too 💞
.
If you’re struggling with addiction of any kind, I invite you to do this exercise. See those old you’s through a lens of love, non judgment and empathy. The guilt and the shame only makes it worse and deepens the cycle 🌀
.
Thank you Strawberry Park Hot Springs for this healing experience that I didn’t even know I needed 🙏🏽
.

You don’t realise how much you have evolved until you come back into your old stomping grounds, where you are face to face with the situations where the old version of you used to be 
.
Coming back to Florida has always been bittersweet for me since I’ve moved away from here about 12 years ago. I was a wild child for the years I lived here, and there are a lot of memories that evoke a lot of heavy emotions when I come back.  Every time I would come back here, I would revert to that old version of myself - the reckless party animal who hated herself when she woke up in the morning. The girl riddled with self doubt and who talked pretty nasty to herself, the one who worried her family and reinforced her wild reputation. I didn’t appreciate this place and blamed people, places and situations here for the way I was behaving. I certainly didn’t appreciate the beauty that’s in our backyard - I took it all for granted and wrote off Florida as “the place I didn’t like to claim that I was from” 
.
But this trip is different. I have a much more clear mind now, and I can see that this place wasn’t the problem - I was. Through the work I have done, I now get to view southwest Florida through a new lens. I am appreciating the friendships and connections that I still have with the people who matter. I am pitching up as a much better version of myself for my family - they aren’t worried about where I snuck out to or where I ended up for the night. And I am loving the beautiful nature we are surrounded by - the radiant sunsets, the lush foliage and beautiful palm trees, the array of birds singing in the morning and the alligators in Lakes Park. I used to feel like I was holding my breath on my visits here, but now I am inhaling and appreciating all the goodness it has to offer 🌴 🐊 
.
So grateful for the work I’ve put in to get to this stage. Changing your mindset can be gruelling sometimes because it consists of little practices that you aren’t sure are having an impact. But then you step into a situation like this and realise how far you’ve come 🙏🏽💫

I had an interesting conversation with someone the other day about the fact that I choose to post pictures of myself wearing minimal clothing on these platforms. It made me realise that my intentions might be being misunderstood, so let me get real 👇🏽
.
It wasn’t that long ago that I actually hated looking at myself in the mirror. I critiqued every inch of my body, but mostly I just couldn’t bare to look myself in the eyes. I was instantly filled with shame, guilt and self loathing. When you’re constantly treating your body like shit and doing things that go against your values when you’re intoxicated, the former emotional states can be a pretty detrimental side effect. Not only that, but I felt pathetic, like I had all this potential that I wasn’t tapping into and was literally just  wasting it all away 🍷
.
Through the work that I have done and the lifestyle I now choose to live, I pulled that inner confidence and self love to the surface, as it definitely wasn’t always there. So these pictures are a reflection of that - please understand the hard work that I have done to feel comfortable enough to post them 💓
.
I also have pretty regimented healthy habits in place, because exercise and nutritious meals are essential for my mental well-being and performance. The physical benefits of that are just a bonus that I am proud to share 🙂
.
If you feel activated by these words or pictures, I invite you to look inside and get curious about why that is. Our triggers can be our greatest teachers 😉
.

Take the time each day to slow down, get back into your body, become aware of the monkey mind. When you start connecting to that true nature within, answers will begin to drop in. Things will start to become clear, and aligned actions for you to take will come into your awareness that you have never thought about before 🌟

What will you do today to connect back to yourself? I’m curious to know 👇🏽

Long Post Alert 🚨 
.
Addiction is a creepy, cunning, manipulative b*tch. It used to tell me lots of stories .. “It’s not that bad” .. “Everyone has nights like that sometimes” .. “I work so hard, I deserve to let loose” .. “I’ll just stick to wine .. “ 
.
.
I woke up to the fact that alcohol wasn’t playing a good role in my life about 5 years ago, and so the sober roller coaster began. I thought if I could just get to 30 days, 60 days, 90 days without a drink, then surely I didn’t have a problem right? 
.
. 
Wrong. I would have these sober stints and things would start to transform in my life and then that one party would come up that I couldn’t resist. Drinking and me would resume our relationship for a little - there would be some fun times - but every time, without fail, it went back to me depending on it for dealing with my emotions and drinking in alcoholic ways. And each time the consequences were getting worse and worse. It was like being in a never ending whirlpool of darkness 🌀 
.
.
They say insanity is doing the same thing over and over and expecting different results. I was a bit insane for those 5 years - The addict in me wanted so badly to cling to my drinking. I desperately wanted to be a “normal drinker”, and I was pretty good at convincing myself and people around me that I was in those periods of returning to drinking. But I was living a double life. On one hand I was teaching yoga, preaching to people to treat their body like a temple and unconditionally love themselves, and the next night I was having a bender, filling my body with toxins and definitely not being loving towards myself. I was even trying to set up a life coaching business to be an example on how to live while I was most certainly not taking my own advice - and wondering why I wasn’t getting anywhere with it 🤣
.
.

I’m so incredibly proud of myself for going home for the holidays without drinking. So many firsts being alcohol free (AF):
- First holiday season AF 
- First vacation AF 
- First international flight and lounge experience AF 
- First time home being AF with my family and friends who have always seen me drink 
.
.
It’s been a journey to say the least, but I can see things way more clearly now. Alcohol doesn’t fit into my dream life like I once believed it did. I can fantasise about fancy bottles of red with my meals or classy cocktails, but the truth is, it doesn’t stop there for me. I end up over doing it more often than not, the hangovers become even more mentally/physically/emotionally taxing, and it always ends up with me leaning on it in unhealthy ways again a couple months after my first initial drink 🥴
.
.
Will I drink again? Who knows, I don’t have a crystal ball to predict the future 🔮 but surviving that trip home without drinking was a huge hurdle for me to get over. I know if I can manage that, I can manage almost anything without drinking 💪🏽
.
.
The best part was showing my family and friends this version of me - my best self. I am so much more calm cool and collected and sure of myself than I have ever been, and damn it feels good 💫
.
.
Day 73 today without a drink. I have taken multiple 30-60 day breaks before, but this time feels different. There has been a shift on a deeper level. I know it’s only holding me back, and fuck anything keeping me away from my dreams 🙅🏼‍♀️
.
.
I know I’m not alone in struggling with this, which is why I choose to be so vocal about it. When you first start to get sober it’s goddamn hard, esp if you’ve had a rockstar party lifestyle past like mine. But it does get easier, and it does take time. And if I can do it, anyone can. My DMs are open for anyone wanting to chat about this, I see you and I’m here for you. We’re in this together ✊🏼

16 years ago today my life changed forever. We were being dumb highschool kids and messing around on my friends car in a parking lot. I ended up flying off the car after it abruptly stopped, landing directly on my head on the concrete. I started vomiting and bleeding out of my ear, a tell tale sign of severe brain damage. They told my friends that I probably wasn’t going to make it.  I got flight for life in a helicopter to the Paediatric Head Trauma Unit in Tampa. My dad had to fight the doctors to let him ride with me because at that point it was unlikely I was going to survive 🤕
.
.
.
By nothing short of a miracle, I walked away pretty unscathed physically - besides loss of taste and smell and partial hearing in my left ear. No paralysis, no severe damage to my intellect or basic functions. After the pounding headache subsided and a few weeks in the hospital, I was sent home to recover 🏠
.
.
.
It quickly became quite apparent that the damage was done on an emotional level. My mood swings became extreme, and my emotionally maturity seemed to have reverted back to toddler years. I remember having temper tantrums when things wouldn’t go my way. Later we got tests done, and the frontal cortex of my brain was most effected when it was rattled around in my skull - the part that’s responsible for rational thinking and decision making 😵‍💫
.
.
.
The years to follow were extremely dark ones. I became super lost, sliding into a life a rebellion, trouble and addiction. The recklessness scale was off the charts - I had more near death experiences. I was never consciously suicidal but a therapist once told me that the way I was behaving was a reflection of someone subconsciously not wanting to be in this life anymore 🥺
.
.
.
This is only a sliver of my story. There’s so much more, and I’m feeling called to share it. I always had this deep knowing my soul was put here this time around to do something BIG. To transform on a profound level, and to help others do the same. That’s why my angels have helped me escape death so many times. I am a warrior goddess. More on this soon 💫

This week in my classes I’ve been talking about expansion. In particular, expanding our joyful experiences. When you have a moment of joy, happiness or love throughout your day, I invite you to stay there. Marinate in it, let it seep into all the cracks of your being. Feel the feels in all your cells, soak it in and stretch it out for as long as you can 💫
.
.
.
If you consciously choose to stay in these blissful moments a few times a day - day after day, week after week, month after month - you will start to literally rewire your brain. You’ll begin to form new neural pathways, little trenches for positive thinking to become your default. Unfortunately we are genetically predisposed for negative thinking - our ancestors needed to remember those negative experiences more intensely than the positive ones in order to survive. But with this method, this expansion of the positive moments, you can re - hardwire your brain for happiness 🌈
.
.
.

When you are trying to make lifestyle and habit changes that are deeply ingrained into your subconscious, it takes time and patience. You have to be ready to change and better multiple levels of your life. Starting with your mind, your psyche - meditation, gratitude journals, therapy, yoga, breathing exercises. Then your physical body - exercise, proper hydration, nourishing food, adequate sleep. Then your close relationships - having a partner who supports and respects you, knowing your worth and setting boundaries to not put up with anything less. Then it trickles out to your home, career, friendship group - making a sacred space where you feel the most safe, choosing a job that fulfils you and feeds your soul, and finding a tribe that inspires you 💞
.
.
.
This all takes time my loves, it doesn’t happen over night. Be patient and know that if you’re making baby steps in the right direction that you’re doing amazing. You’re right where you’re meant to be. Keep on keepin on 😉

Let’s talk about addiction. It probably runs way more rampant through our society than you think. The silent killer that a lot of people don’t want to talk about or acknowledge. The thing that eats people alive with shame and guilt. It can come in many different shapes and sizes. Food, drugs, sex, gambling, alcohol, social media, sugar, pretzels 🥨 (true story that’s me hahaha). The more I learn about it, the more I think we’re all a little bit addicted to something in someway. It is something that I have personally struggled with most of my life. I was always the party girl but a lot of people didn’t realise behind all those sweet dance moves 😉💃🏽 and late nights there was a broken little girl. This year I’ve gotten sober curious and it’s been such an eye-opening journey. I’ve slipped up a few times, it’s not always a straight road. I’m not perfect. But I’m learning, learning to love and accept all parts of me 💗
.
.
.
I was nominated by the gorgeous @itsnotmeitsbooze to raise 3 fingers for addiction awareness. To help break down the stigma and make us realise it’s okay to not be okay. It’s okay to struggle. Our society kinda sets us up for it in a fucked up way. But I promise that if you reach out and talk about it with someone in a similar boat, you won’t feel so alone. So my door is always open. DM me if you’re feeling down or you’re riding the struggle bus. Looking back at the last decade of my life with amazement 🎠

Sometimes I get caught up in the day to day bullshit and I forget how far I have come. All the twists and turns, the rainbow-and-butterfly moments, and the gut wrenching, never-thought-I-was-gonna-make-it-through-this times. The belly laughs, the wildly fun dancing nights, and then the sobering moments where I’ve questioned everything about my existence. The super secure times where I’ve been settled, and the adventurous, wanderlust-filled, exotic plane, train and automobile rides where I’ve lost and found myself all over again 🎡

So incredibly grateful for the 2010’s. It is here, in your sliver of time, where I have started to blossom into the woman I know I am destined to become. I can now look at my reflection in the mirror with confidence; and whisper “I love you” to that girl I see looking back at me (which took me the better part of this decade to be able to do) 🥰

This has been the decade of exploring - not only out into our wild, wonderful world all of us get to call home, but diving into a deep, inward exploration as well 🧘🏼‍♂️ Being blessed enough to get to travel our globe and immerse myself into so many different cultures, but also getting to really know, love and accept all aspects of me - the good, the bad, and the ugly 👁‍🗨 2020 - new decade on the horizon - I am beyond stoked for what you will bring. The last two weeks of trekking the Annapurna Circuit has probably been the most physically and mentally tough task I’ve ever voluntarily put myself through. 150+ km of walking with my backpack, plus many more kilometres in insanely bumpy jeep and tiny plane rides (I had to come back early because my knee didn’t like all the craziness), hanging out at 5000 metres elevation more than a few times and crossing Thorong-La pass (5500 metres) was no joke! Sweat and tears were very common, but the unbelievably breathtaking views make it all worth it. I’ve never been in mountains this grandiose, the energy was unreal. Here’s to a achievement I will never forget and always be super proud to say that I’ve accomplished 💪🏼🏆 they don’t even begin to do justice, but more pics coming soon 🏔

This pose has been resonating with me lots lately. Virabhadrasana ll (Warrior 2) represents the focused attention and warrior strength required to prepare for battle (no, I didn’t join the army haha). When we practice yoga, our mat can represent the battlefield, with our minds becoming the “enemy”. It’s a daily struggle for me to turn off the negative voice in my head telling me all sorts of bullshit that really brings me down if I let it take control. It’s messed up! My daily meditation/breath work and sober mind has been helping me deal with little Miss Negative Nancy but I’ve been learning that she will always be there to some extent - but it’s how you handle her that will determine how loud she is. I’ve been trying not to let myself get wrapped up in those thoughts when they come. I acknowledge them, take note of how they make me feel, and then politely tell them to fuck off 🖕🏽
.
.
.
.
Hope that helped anyone who struggles with Miss Little Negative Nancy too. Shut the Bitch down 🙅🏼‍♀️ and remember how amazing you are 🤗🌈✨🦄
.
.
